high.title: S&P Expects One More BSP Rate Increase This Year
high.summary: S&P Global Ratings has signaled that the BSP is not done tightening, projecting one additional rate hike that would bring the benchmark policy rate to 5.00% by end-2026. S&P Asia-Pacific Senior Economist Vishrut Rana delivered the forecast on One News, framing it as "modest further tightening" while cautioning that prolonged elevated rates risk dampening domestic demand over the medium term. For PHP traders, a confirmed BSP hike cycle continuation is broadly supportive of the peso, narrowing the real rate differential with the USD and reducing capital outflow pressure. For bond investors, this is a clear bear signal at the short end of the yield curve — expect T-bill and short-tenor GS yields to remain elevated or edge higher into the next Monetary Board meeting. Critically, this aligns with the hawkish tone already being priced in at the latest T-bill auction (see Article 1). Key watch points: the timing of the next Monetary Board meeting, any BSP guidance on the inflation trajectory, and whether the Fed's own hawkish posture compresses or widens the BSP's room to act independently.

high.title: Yields on Short-Term Gov't Debt End Higher on Hawkish BSP, Fed
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury fully awarded P90 billion in combined Cash Management Bills (CMBs) and Treasury bills at Monday's auction, with total tenders reaching P178.888 billion — a healthy bid-to-cover ratio signaling robust demand even as yields moved higher. The dual hawkish signals from both the BSP and the US Federal Reserve are the primary drivers pushing short-end yields upward, compounded by ongoing uncertainty from the unresolved Middle East conflict, which sustains risk-aversion and inflationary commodity price pressures. For bond portfolio managers, the full award confirms the BTr had no need to reject bids, but the higher clearing yields represent mark-to-market losses on existing short-duration holdings. The strong oversubscription (P178.9B tendered vs. P90B offered) does, however, indicate that local and offshore investors still see Philippine short-term paper as attractive at current yield levels — a constructive sign for near-term GS market liquidity. Traders should monitor upcoming auction results for the 5- and 10-year tenors to assess how far the hawkish repricing is transmitting along the curve. The persistence of Middle East geopolitical risk remains an upside risk to oil prices and, by extension, Philippine inflation and BSP policy.

high.title: Peso Climbs as US and Iran Set to Resume Talks
high.summary: The Philippine peso appreciated 12 centavos to close at P61.17/USD on Monday, recovering from Friday's P61.29 close, driven by improved risk sentiment after the US and Iran agreed to halt hostilities and resume peace negotiations. The intraday range was P61.125 (high) to P61.32 (low), with the session opening slightly weaker at P61.30 before buyers took control. This geopolitically-driven PHP strengthening is meaningful for FX traders: the peso had been under pressure partly due to the Middle East conflict's upward push on global oil prices — a key vulnerability for the Philippines given its heavy crude import dependence. A sustained de-escalation in the Middle East would be structurally bullish for the PHP through two channels: (1) lower oil import bills narrowing the trade deficit, and (2) reduced global risk-off sentiment improving capital flow dynamics for emerging market currencies. However, the near-term ceiling on PHP appreciation remains the hawkish Fed, which constrains the USD's downside. Traders should watch the P61.00 level as the next psychological support for USD/PHP, and any breakdown in US-Iran talks as a key tail risk that could rapidly reverse today's gains. BSP intervention activity, if any, should also be monitored at stronger PHP levels.

medium.title: World Bank Approves $1.02-Billion Loan for Philippine Energy Transition and Water Security
medium.summary:
The World Bank has approved a $1.02-billion Development Policy Loan (DPL) to support the Philippines' clean energy transition and water security reforms, comprising a $1-billion IBRD loan and a smaller concessional tranche. While primarily a structural/sectoral story, this is moderately relevant to macro and FX watchers: the loan represents a significant external financing inflow that will support the Philippines' balance of payments and could modestly bolster the BSP's foreign reserve position upon disbursement. Additionally, the energy transition focus is relevant to the Philippine inflation and trade balance outlook — if successful, reducing the country's dependence on volatile imported fossil fuels would structurally compress the current account deficit and reduce a key source of PHP depreciation pressure over the medium term. Fund managers should note this as a positive sovereign credit signal, potentially supportive of Philippine GS spreads.

medium.title: PSE Index Rises on IPO News, Easing US-Iran Woes
medium.summary:
The PSEi climbed 1.0% or 61.17 points to close at 6,133.41, reclaiming the 6,100 level, while the broader All Shares Index gained 0.67% to 3,352.96. The rally was driven by a dual catalyst: improving geopolitical sentiment as US-Iran tensions eased, and renewed investor optimism around fresh IPO developments in the local market. For equity-focused fund managers, the breach back above 6,100 is a technically constructive signal, suggesting near-term buying interest. The IPO pipeline is a positive structural story for the PSEi as new listings can deepen market breadth and attract incremental foreign participation. International investors should monitor whether foreign net buying accompanied this move — sustained foreign inflows would provide additional PHP support and reinforce the bullish tone. Watch the 6,200 resistance level as the next meaningful test.
